title: Microsoft Entra: sensitivity labels for cloud security groups
summary: The briefing's rollout dates, separate tenant enablement, preview limitations and documented controls are supported. Minor corrections should acknowledge conflicting general licensing guidance, clarify the Purview PowerShell control, tidy the control paths and Graph call, and align the checklist with its controls table.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans sensitivity label assignment for Microsoft Entra cloud security groups.
claims.quote: Apply sensitivity labels to Microsoft Entra cloud security groups to extend the classification and governance you already use for Microsoft 365 groups.

claims.claim: Cloud security groups use the same published labels configured for groups and sites.
claims.quote: The same labels you publish in the Microsoft Purview portal and configure for groups and sites apply automatically to cloud security groups

claims.claim: The roadmap says no separate label configuration is required.
claims.quote: with no separate label configuration required.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development"

claims.claim: The notice lists the Microsoft Entra admin center, Azure portal, PowerShell and Microsoft Graph as assignment surfaces.

claims.claim: The notice allows assignment during creation or after a group has been created.
claims.quote: Administrators will be able to apply published Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels to cloud security groups during group creation or after a group has been created.

claims.claim: The notice says no action is required to receive the change.
claims.quote: No action is required to receive this change.

claims.claim: The notice requires independent tenant enablement for cloud security groups even when Microsoft 365 group labels are enabled.
claims.quote: If sensitivity labels are already enabled for Microsoft 365 groups, note that cloud security groups require a separate configuration setting and must be enabled independently.

claims.claim: Label-based protection already exists for Microsoft 365 groups and SharePoint sites.
claims.quote: This capability extends label-based protection currently available for Microsoft 365 groups and SharePoint sites to cloud security groups.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The feature is admin-opt-in and changes no cloud security group label enforcement until enabled.
claims.quote: To apply sensitivity labels to cloud security groups, you must enable the feature by creating or updating tenant-level directory settings.

claims.claim: Tenant settings use Group.Security separately from the Group.Unified template for Microsoft 365 groups.
claims.quote: Cloud security groups use the `Group.Security` settings template, which is separate from the `Group.Unified` template used for Microsoft 365 groups.

claims.claim: New-MgBetaDirectorySetting -BodyParameter $params enables labels with templateId d209f6fa-3839-4d70-b83f-60b1c64d0e8f and EnableMIPLabels=True.
claims.quote:
templateId = "d209f6fa-3839-4d70-b83f-60b1c64d0e8f"
name = "EnableMIPLabels"
value = "True"
New-MgBetaDirectorySetting -BodyParameter $params

claims.claim: Existing directory settings are changed with Update-MgBetaDirectorySetting.
claims.quote:
If the settings already exist and you need to update them:
Update-MgBetaDirectorySetting -DirectorySettingId $Setting.Id `
    -BodyParameter $params

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls; Open questions: tenant toggle
claims.claim: No admin-center toggle is documented for tenant enablement of security-group sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: Searched: "cloud security groups" "EnableMIPLabels" "admin center" enable. Opened Entra groups-sensitivity-labels; search and feature page document Group.Security PowerShell settings, not an admin-center enablement toggle.

claims.claim: Existing groups are labelled in Microsoft Entra admin center > Microsoft Entra ID > Groups > All groups > group > Properties > Sensitivity label.
claims.quote:
Select Microsoft Entra ID.
Select Groups > All groups, and then select the group you want to label.
On the group's page, select Properties.
Select a sensitivity label from the Sensitivity label dropdown.

claims.claim: PATCH /v1.0/groups/{id} assigns a security group's label through assignedLabels.
claims.quote:
PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/groups/0d09007d-45b2-458c-b180-880dde3a302e
This property can be specified during group creation or update. However, for cloud security groups, it's immutable once set.
claims.fix: Set controls[1].api.call to 'PATCH /v1.0/groups/{id}' and append to the note: 'The request body sets the assignedLabels collection with the label ID.' Make the same presentation change in the rendered table.

claims.claim: Group.ManageProtection.All is the delegated permission for setting assignedLabels on cloud security groups.
claims.quote: Group.ManageProtection.All delegated permission is the least privileged permission to update the assignedLabels property for cloud security groups.

claims.claim: App-only assignment of assignedLabels on cloud security groups is not supported.
claims.quote: App-only scenarios aren't supported.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Scope: Prerequisites; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Execute-AzureADLabelSync synchronises sensitivity labels to Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: Use the Execute-AzureADLabelSync cmdlet to start the synchronization of sensitivity labels into Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.claim: An admin UI control for synchronising published labels to Microsoft Entra ID is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "sensitivity labels" "synchronize" "portal" "Execute-AzureADLabelSync". Read Execute-AzureADLabelSync, Entra groups-sensitivity-labels and the Purview container-sync search excerpt; all prescribe PowerShell, with no UI sync control.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance controls: third row; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Execute-AzureADLabelSync runs only in Security & Compliance PowerShell, not the Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK.
claims.quote: The `Execute-AzureADLabelSync` cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell, not in the Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Scope: Prerequisites; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Labels can take up to 24 hours after synchronisation to become available.
claims.quote: Labels can take up to 24 hours after synchronization to become available.

claims.claim: The label-management route is Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels
To edit an existing label, select it, and then select the Edit label icon.
claims.fix: For the existing-label editing route, extend controls[3].ui.path to 'Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > label > Edit label'. Update the rendered table to match; retain the note about selecting the Groups & Sites scope.

claims.claim: Set-Label -Identity <label> -SiteAndGroupProtectionEnabled <$true|$false> enables or disables the label's Site and Group Protection action.
claims.quote:
The SiteAndGroupProtectionEnabled parameter enables or disables the Site and Group Protection action for the label. Valid values are:
$true: The Site and Group Protection action is enabled.
$false: The Site and Group Protection action is disabled.

claims.claim: The general Purview Set-Label control is presented as not confirmed for cloud security groups.
claims.quote: You can now use Security & Compliance PowerShell to create and configure all the settings you see in your labeling admin center.
claims.fix: Replace the uncertainty in controls[3].note and the final Governance controls paragraph with: 'General Purview control: Set-Label modifies the published label; SiteAndGroupProtectionEnabled enables or disables its Site and Group Protection action. Cloud security groups use the same labels configured for groups and sites.' Retain the Groups & Sites scope instruction.

claims.claim: No control is documented to change or remove an assigned security-group sensitivity label during preview.
claims.quote: Searched: "cloud security groups" "change or remove" sensitivity label. Opened Entra groups-sensitivity-labels and Graph group-update: the former prohibits modification/removal during preview; the latter says assignedLabels is immutable once set.

claims.claim: Learn's workaround for the wrong label is a new security group with the correct label and re-added members.
claims.quote: To change a label, create a new security group with the correct label, and then re-add the members to the new group.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Learn requires at least one active Entra ID P1 or P2 licence, or Microsoft 365 E3/E5, in the organisation.
claims.quote: Your organization has at least one active Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 license (or Microsoft 365 E3/E5).

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Licensing is included in the eligible existing subscriptions.
claims.quote:
Sensitivity labeling, including automatic or policy-based labeling, requires a Microsoft 365 E5 license or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance (IPG).
Manual Sensitivity Labeling | Included | Included | Included | Included | Included
claims.fix: Retain included and the feature page's prerequisites. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/microsoft-365-service-descriptions/microsoft-365-tenantlevel-services-licensing-guidance/microsoft-purview-service-description and add: 'The service description lists manual sensitivity labelling as included in Microsoft 365 E3/E5, but also contains a broader statement that sensitivity labelling requires Microsoft 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance (IPG); the feature page specifically lists Entra ID P1/P2 or Microsoft 365 E3/E5.'

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no separate feature price or meter beyond the stated subscription prerequisites.
claims.quote: Searched: "cloud security groups" sensitivity labels pricing license meter. Read feature prerequisites and Purview service description sensitivity-labeling section; subscription requirements are documented, but no separate security-group label price or meter was found.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: During preview the listed high-privilege roles, including Global Administrator, User Administrator and Groups Administrator, can bypass label policy on member additions.
claims.quote:
The following admin roles and application permissions can bypass label policy enforcement when adding members.
Admin roles: Global Administrator, User Administrator, Groups Administrator

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: During preview apps with Group.ReadWrite.All, Directory.ReadWrite.All, Directory.ReadWriteAdvanced.All or GroupMember.ReadWrite.All can bypass label policy on member additions.
claims.quote: Application permissions: `Group.ReadWrite.All`, `Directory.ReadWrite.All`, `Directory.ReadWriteAdvanced.All`, `GroupMember.ReadWrite.All`

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope: Who and what is covered
claims.claim: This release supports assigned-membership cloud security groups, not dynamic-membership security groups.
claims.quote: The group is a Cloud Security group with assigned membership type (not dynamic).

claims.claim: A label can be applied to a dynamic group in some edge cases, but its policy is not enforced.
claims.quote: While there are certain edge cases where you can apply a label to a dynamic group, the associated label policy isn't enforced.

claims.claim: Security groups synced from on-premises Active Directory are unsupported.
claims.quote: Security groups synced from on-premises Active Directory and Exchange-managed security groups aren't supported.

claims.quote: Security groups synced from on-premises Active Directory and Exchange-managed security groups aren't supported.

claims.claim: Mail-enabled security groups are unsupported.

claims.where: Scope: Who and what is covered
claims.claim: Distribution lists are unsupported.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labels for mail-enabled security groups and distribution lists aren't supported.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: A security group containing nested groups cannot be labelled until they are removed.
claims.quote: You can't label a group that currently contains nested groups. To label a parent group, remove all nested (child) groups first

claims.claim: Child groups must carry labels at least as restrictive as the parent's.
claims.quote: When you add a child group back to a labeled parent, the child group's label must be at least as restrictive as the parent's label.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center does not support assigning sensitivity labels to security groups.
claims.quote: Assigning sensitivity labels to security groups isn't supported in the Microsoft 365 admin center or in the My Groups portal.

claims.claim: The My Groups portal does not support assigning sensitivity labels to security groups.
claims.quote: Assigning sensitivity labels to security groups isn't supported in the Microsoft 365 admin center or in the My Groups portal.

claims.claim: Existing guests can conflict with applying a guest-blocking label.
claims.quote: Applying a label that blocks guest access to a group that contains guest members. Resolution: Remove the guest members, then apply the label.
